questions.question: Which declaration represents the standard document type for HTML5?
questions.explanation: In HTML5, the doctype is simplified to <!DOCTYPE html>. It ensures the browser renders the page in standards mode.

questions.question: Which HTML element is considered the root element of an HTML page?
questions.explanation: The <html> element is the root element that wraps all content on the entire page.

questions.question: What kind of information does the <head> element contain?
questions.a: The main visual content of the website
questions.b: Metadata, title, and links to scripts/styles
questions.explanation: The <head> contains machine-readable information (metadata) about the document, like its title, scripts, and style sheets.

questions.question: Which attribute is used inside the <html> tag to declare the language of the Web page?
questions.explanation: The 'lang' attribute (e.g., <html lang="en">) declares the primary language of the document for accessibility and search engines.

questions.question: Is HTML tag syntax strictly case-sensitive in HTML5?
questions.a: Yes, all tags must be lowercase
questions.b: Yes, all tags must be uppercase
questions.c: No, it is case-insensitive, but lowercase is recommended
questions.d: No, but attributes must be uppercase
questions.explanation:
HTML5 is case-insensitive (e.g.,

and

both work), but the W3C recommends lowercase for cleaner, consistent code.

questions.question: What is an 'empty' (or void) HTML element?
questions.a: An element that contains no text but has child elements
questions.b: An element without a closing tag and no content
questions.c: An element that is hidden via CSS
questions.explanation:
Empty elements, like
,
, and , have no content and do not require a closing tag.

questions.question: Which <meta> tag declaration ensures the browser uses the correct character encoding?
questions.explanation: <meta charset="UTF-8"> is the standard way to set character encoding, supporting almost all characters and symbols globally.

questions.question: According to HTML5 standards, is the <title> element strictly required within the <head>?
questions.b: Yes, it is mandatory for a valid HTML document
questions.c: Only if the page is being indexed by search engines
questions.d: Yes, but only if there is no <h1> element
questions.explanation: The HTML standard requires a <title> element inside the <head> block for the document to be valid.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to define the most important heading on a page?
questions.explanation: <h1> defines the most important heading. <h6> is the least important.

questions.question: Which tag defines a paragraph?
questions.explanation:
The

tag defines a paragraph. Browsers automatically add margin before and after a

element.

questions.question: How do you insert a single line break without starting a new paragraph?
questions.explanation:
The
tag inserts a single line break. It is an empty element.

questions.question: What is the semantic purpose of the <hr> tag in HTML5?
questions.a: To draw a purely decorative horizontal line
questions.b: To define a thematic break in the content
questions.c: To hide the text below it
questions.d: To act as a hard return for text wrapping
questions.explanation: In HTML5, <hr> represents a thematic break between paragraph-level elements, not just a visual line.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between <b> and <strong>?
questions.a: <b> makes text bigger; <strong> makes it bolder
questions.b: <b> is for styling; <strong> indicates semantic importance
questions.c: There is no difference in modern HTML
questions.explanation: Both render text bold by default, but <strong> conveys extra importance/urgency to screen readers, whereas <b> is just for visual attention.

questions.question: Which tag is used to display preformatted text, preserving both spaces and line breaks?
questions.explanation: The <pre> tag preserves both spaces and line breaks, typically rendering in a fixed-width font.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax for adding a comment in HTML?
questions.explanation: HTML comments start with <!-- and end with -->.

questions.question: Which tag defines text that has been inserted into a document (often styled with an underline)?
questions.explanation: <ins> defines inserted text. While <u> also underlines, <ins> carries semantic meaning about document edits.

questions.question: Which tag is used for subscript text, such as the '2' in H2O?
questions.explanation: <sub> defines subscript text, which appears half a character below the normal line.

questions.question: Which element defines a section that is quoted from another source?
questions.explanation: <blockquote> is used for long quotations, usually indented by browsers. <q> is for short, inline quotes.

questions.question: Which attribute is used to apply inline CSS styles directly to an HTML element?
questions.explanation:
The 'style' attribute specifies inline CSS rules for an element (e.g.,

).

questions.question: Where should the <style> tag typically be placed for internal CSS?
questions.a: At the very end of the <body>
questions.explanation: Internal stylesheets using the <style> tag should be defined inside the <head> element.

questions.question: Which statement about the 'id' attribute is strictly true?
questions.a: An 'id' value must be unique within the entire HTML document
questions.b: Multiple elements can share the same 'id' if they are different tags
questions.c: An 'id' must begin with a number
questions.d: An 'id' cannot be used for CSS styling, only JavaScript
questions.explanation: The 'id' attribute specifies a unique identifier; no two elements on the same page can have the same id.

questions.question: How can you assign multiple classes to a single HTML element?
questions.explanation: Multiple classes are separated by a space within the same class attribute.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to link an external CSS stylesheet?
questions.explanation: The <link> tag (e.g., <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">) is used to link external stylesheets.

questions.question: What is a 'Global Attribute' in HTML?
questions.a: An attribute that must be placed in the <html> tag
questions.b: An attribute that can be used on any HTML element
questions.c: An attribute that translates content into multiple languages
questions.d: An attribute used exclusively for geographical location data
questions.explanation: Global attributes (like class, id, style, title, lang) can be applied to almost any HTML element.

questions.question: In standard CSS specificity, which attribute takes precedence if both style an element?
questions.d: Whichever is listed first in the HTML tag
questions.explanation: An 'id' selector has higher specificity than a 'class' selector in CSS.

questions.question: Which global attribute provides a tooltip when a user hovers over an element?
questions.explanation: The 'title' attribute specifies extra information about an element, typically displayed as a tooltip on hover.

questions.question: Which tag is used to create a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag is used to define a hyperlink to another page or resource.

questions.question: Which attribute of the <a> tag indicates the link's destination?
questions.explanation: The 'href' (Hypertext Reference) attribute contains the URL destination of the link.

questions.question: How do you make a link open in a new tab or window?
questions.explanation: Setting target="_blank" forces the browser to open the linked document in a new tab or window.

questions.question: What happens when the href attribute contains a value like href="#contact"?
questions.a: It throws an invalid URL error
questions.b: It links to a page named contact.html
questions.c: It jumps to the element on the same page with id="contact"
questions.d: It opens a new email draft to 'contact'
questions.explanation: The hash symbol (#) creates a bookmark link, jumping to the element with that specific id on the current page.

questions.question: Which href value creates a link that opens the user's default email client?
questions.explanation: The 'mailto:' scheme inside an href opens the user's email program to send a message to that address.

questions.question: What is the difference between an absolute URL and a relative URL?
questions.a: Absolute URLs only work on the internet; relative URLs only work locally
questions.b: Absolute URLs include the full web address (e.g., https://...); relative URLs point to a file within the same site
questions.c: Absolute URLs are for images; relative URLs are for text
questions.explanation: Absolute URLs contain the protocol and domain. Relative URLs describe the path relative to the current file structure.

questions.question: By default, how do web browsers visually represent an unvisited link?
questions.explanation: The standard browser default for an unvisited link is underlined blue text. Visited links become purple.

questions.question: How do you use an image as a link?
questions.explanation: You nest the tag inside the tag to make the image clickable.

questions.question: Which attribute is required to specify the path to the image in an tag?
questions.explanation: The 'src' (source) attribute specifies the path or URL to the image file.

questions.question: Why is the 'alt' attribute crucial for images?
questions.a: It makes the image load faster
questions.b: It provides alternative text if the image fails to load and for screen readers
questions.explanation: The 'alt' attribute provides semantic meaning for accessibility (screen readers) and acts as a visual fallback if the network fails.

questions.question: What happens if you define both 'width' and 'height' attributes on an tag?
questions.a: The browser reserves space for the image before it loads, preventing layout shifts
questions.b: The browser overrides CSS rules associated with the image
questions.c: The image is automatically compressed in file size
questions.d: The image becomes responsive to the screen width
questions.explanation: Setting width and height attributes reserves the correct layout space, preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) as the page loads.

questions.question: Which tag allows you to specify different image sources depending on the user's screen size or format support?
questions.explanation: The <picture> element works with <source> child elements to provide art direction (different crops for mobile vs desktop) or format switching (e.g., WebP vs JPEG).

questions.question: Inside a <picture> element, which tag is used to specify the alternative media files?
questions.explanation: The <source> element is used inside <picture> (and <audio>/<video>) to specify media resources and their media queries/types.

questions.question: Which attribute delays the loading of an image until it is close to the viewport?
questions.explanation: The loading="lazy" attribute instructs the browser to defer loading the image until it enters or is about to enter the visible viewport.

questions.question: How do you add a favicon to a website?
questions.explanation: Favicons are added in the <head> using the <link> tag with rel="icon".

questions.question: What is an HTML Image Map?
questions.a: An image generated dynamically via JavaScript
questions.b: An image with clickable areas linking to different destinations
questions.c: A map embedded from Google Maps
questions.d: An SVG image that scales infinitely
questions.explanation: Image maps (using <map> and <area> tags) define clickable regions (coords) over a single image.

questions.question: Which attribute links an to a element?
questions.explanation: The 'usemap' attribute on the tag points to the 'name' attribute of a element (e.g., usemap="#planetmap").

questions.question: Is an image defined via CSS 'background-image' read by screen readers by default?
questions.a: Yes, screen readers analyze all background images
questions.b: No, background images are strictly decorative and ignored by screen readers
questions.c: Yes, but only if the filename is descriptive
questions.d: No, unless an alt attribute is added to the CSS
questions.explanation: CSS background images are treated as visual decoration. If an image contains crucial information, an HTML tag with an 'alt' attribute must be used.

questions.question: Which tag defines an HTML table?
questions.explanation: The <table> tag is the container for all other table elements like rows and data cells.

questions.question: Which tag is used to define a standard data cell in a table?
questions.explanation: The <td> (table data) tag defines a standard cell containing data within a table row.

questions.question: What is the visual difference between a <th> and a <td> element by default?
questions.b: <th> text is bold and centered; <td> is normal and left-aligned
questions.c: <th> cells have borders; <td> cells do not
questions.d: There is no default visual difference
questions.explanation: Browsers render <th> (table header) text as bold and centered to distinguish it from regular <td> data.

questions.question: Which attribute allows a single table cell to span across multiple columns?
questions.explanation: The 'colspan' attribute (e.g., <td colspan="2">) merges adjacent cells horizontally across columns.

questions.question: Which attribute allows a table cell to span across multiple rows?
questions.explanation: The 'rowspan' attribute allows a single cell to stretch vertically across multiple rows.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to add a title or explanation above an HTML table?
questions.explanation: The <caption> tag must be inserted immediately after the <table> tag and provides a title for the table.

questions.question: What are the correct tags to group the header, body, and footer content of a table?
questions.explanation: <thead>, <tbody>, and <tfoot> group table rows semantically, which is useful for CSS styling and printing long tables across pages.

questions.question: Is it possible to nest another complete <table> inside a <td> element?
questions.a: Yes, HTML allows tables to be nested inside table data cells
questions.b: No, nesting tables invalidates the HTML structure
questions.c: Yes, but only if the nested table has no <th> elements
questions.d: No, tables can only be nested inside <div> elements
questions.explanation: Table data cells (<td>) can contain almost any HTML element, including entire nested tables.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <colgroup> and <col> elements?
questions.a: To group columns together for shared CSS styling without applying styles to every cell
questions.b: To merge columns together like the colspan attribute
questions.c: To define the data type (text, number, date) of a column
questions.d: To make columns responsive and collapse on mobile devices
questions.explanation: <colgroup> specifies a group of one or more columns (<col>) for formatting. It prevents having to repeat CSS classes on every <td>.

questions.question: How does the 'scope' attribute improve table accessibility?
questions.a: It highlights the active cell for screen readers
questions.b: It tells screen readers if a <th> is a header for a row, column, row group, or col group
questions.c: It forces the table to fit within the viewport scope
questions.d: It links a table caption to a specific cell
questions.explanation: Using scope="col" or scope="row" on a <th> element explicitly associates the header with its corresponding data cells for assistive technologies.

questions.question: Which tag creates a bulleted (unordered) list?
questions.explanation: The <ul> (unordered list) tag creates a list where items are typically marked with bullets.

questions.question: Which tag creates a numbered (ordered) list?
questions.explanation: The <ol> (ordered list) tag creates a list where items are marked with numbers or letters.

questions.question: Which tag is used to define an individual item within both <ul> and <ol> lists?
questions.explanation: The <li> tag defines a list item.

questions.question: How do you change an ordered list to use uppercase Roman numerals (I, II, III)?
questions.explanation: The type attribute on an <ol> (e.g., type="I", type="a", type="1") changes the numbering marker.

questions.question: Which attribute allows an ordered list to begin counting from a number other than 1?
questions.explanation: The 'start' attribute specifies the numeric starting value of an ordered list (e.g., <ol start="50">).

questions.question: How do you make an ordered list count downwards (3, 2, 1)?
questions.explanation: The boolean attribute 'reversed' specifies that the list order should be descending.

questions.question: Which three tags are required to create a description list (like a dictionary)?
questions.explanation: <dl> defines the description list, <dt> defines the term, and <dd> describes/defines the term.

questions.question: What is the fundamental layout difference between <div> and <span>?
questions.a: <div> is for text; <span> is for images
questions.b: <div> is an inline element; <span> is a block-level element
questions.c: <div> is a block-level element; <span> is an inline element
questions.d: There is no difference; they are interchangeable
questions.explanation: <div> always starts on a new line and takes up full width (block). <span> does not start a new line and only takes up necessary width (inline).

questions.question: What does 'Semantic HTML' mean?
questions.a: Using HTML tags that describe the meaning of the content, not just its appearance
questions.b: Using HTML combined with a semantic CSS framework like Bootstrap
questions.c: Writing HTML in strict alphabetical order
questions.d: Creating HTML pages that are entirely accessible without CSS
questions.explanation: Semantic HTML elements (like <header>, <article>, <form>) clearly describe their meaning to both the browser and the developer.

questions.question: Which semantic element is typically used to group introductory content or a set of navigational links at the top of a page?
questions.explanation: The <header> element represents a container for introductory content or a set of navigational links.

questions.question: Which tag should wrap a block of major navigation links on a website?
questions.explanation: The <nav> element defines a set of navigation links. It is intended only for major blocks of navigation.

questions.question: Which tag represents content that is tangentially related to the content around it, often displayed as a sidebar?
questions.explanation: The <aside> element is used for content loosely related to the primary content, such as sidebars, pull quotes, or ads.

questions.question: What is the correct semantic element for a self-contained composition in a document, such as a blog post or news story?
questions.explanation: The <article> element specifies independent, self-contained content that should make sense on its own (e.g., a forum post or news article).

questions.question: What distinguishes the <main> element from other semantic tags like <section> or <article>?
questions.a: It automatically centers content on the screen
questions.b: There should only be one visible <main> element per document
questions.d: It replaces the <body> element in HTML5
questions.explanation: The <main> tag specifies the dominant content of the <body>. A document must not have more than one <main> element visible.

questions.question: Which element defines the authorship, copyright, or contact information for its nearest sectioning element or page?
questions.explanation: The <footer> element typically contains authorship information, copyright data, and related documents links.

questions.question: When should you use a <section> element instead of a <div>?
questions.a: When the content needs a border
questions.b: When the content represents a thematic grouping usually with its own heading
questions.c: When the content contains forms or inputs
questions.d: When you want the content to be inline rather than block-level
questions.explanation: <section> is a semantic block for a thematic grouping of content (typically with a heading). <div> has no semantic meaning and is strictly for styling/layout.

questions.question: Which two tags work together to create an interactive 'accordion' widget that users can click to open and close?
questions.explanation: <details> creates an interactive widget that the user can open/close. <summary> provides the visible heading that the user clicks.

questions.question: How do semantic layout elements directly benefit SEO (Search Engine Optimization)?
questions.a: They execute faster in the browser engine
questions.b: They help search engines understand the structure, context, and hierarchy of the content
questions.c: They hide keywords from users while showing them to search bots
questions.explanation: Search engines use semantic tags to better index the page by understanding which parts are navigation, main content, or side notes.

questions.question: Which HTML element is used to create a document section containing interactive controls for submitting information?
questions.explanation: The <form> tag defines a form that is used to collect user input.

questions.question: Which attribute of the <form> tag specifies the URL where the form data should be sent?
questions.explanation: The 'action' attribute specifies the URL/URI of the file or server endpoint that processes the submitted form data.

questions.question: Which form method appends form data directly into the URL as name/value pairs?
questions.explanation: The GET method appends the form data to the URL (e.g., /page?name=john). It is not secure for sensitive data.

questions.question: Why should the POST method always be used when sending passwords or sensitive data?
questions.a: Because POST data is encrypted by the browser automatically
questions.b: Because POST sends data in the HTTP request body, keeping it out of browser history and URLs
questions.d: Because POST data cannot be intercepted by hackers
questions.explanation: POST appends form data inside the body of the HTTP request, preventing sensitive info from being visible in the URL, bookmarks, or browser history.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the <label> element?
questions.a: To make text bold and red next to a form input
questions.b: To group multiple form fields together inside a box
questions.c: To define a clickable text label linked to a specific form control, improving usability
questions.d: To validate the data entered by the user
questions.explanation: Labels improve accessibility and usability. Clicking a linked <label> automatically focuses its associated form input.

questions.question: How do you correctly bind a <label> to a specific <input> element?
questions.a: The <label> 'for' attribute must match the <input> 'name' attribute
questions.b: The <label> 'for' attribute must match the <input> 'id' attribute
questions.c: The <input> must be placed strictly before the <label> tag
questions.d: The <label> 'bind' attribute must match the <input> 'id' attribute
questions.explanation: The 'for' attribute of the <label> tag must be equal to the 'id' attribute of the related element to bind them together.

questions.question: Why is the 'name' attribute essential for <input> elements within a form?
questions.b: It is required for the browser to render the input box
questions.c: Without a 'name' attribute, the input's data will NOT be sent when the form is submitted
questions.d: It provides placeholder text inside the input
questions.explanation: Form data is sent as name/value pairs. If an input lacks a 'name' attribute, its value is ignored during submission.

questions.question: What is the default behavior of a web page when a user clicks an <input type="submit">?
questions.a: The form data is sent and the browser reloads or navigates to the action URL
questions.b: The form data is sent silently in the background via AJAX
questions.c: The form clears all fields but stays on the same page
questions.d: The browser opens a confirmation popup
questions.explanation: By default, form submission triggers a full page reload or navigation to the URL specified in the action attribute.

questions.question: Which input type creates a single-line text field?
questions.explanation: <input type="text"> is the default form control for single-line text entry.

questions.question: Which input type visually masks the characters entered by the user (usually replacing them with dots or asterisks)?
questions.explanation: <input type="password"> obscures the entered text for basic visual security.

questions.question: How do you group radio buttons so that selecting one automatically deselects the others?
questions.a: Give them all the same 'id' attribute
questions.b: Give them all the same 'class' attribute
questions.c: Give them all the same 'name' attribute
questions.explanation: Radio buttons (<input type="radio">) are mutually exclusive when they share the exact same 'name' attribute.

questions.question: Which input type allows the user to select ZERO or MORE options from a predefined list?
questions.explanation: Checkboxes allow users to select multiple options independent of one another.

questions.question: Which element creates a drop-down selection menu?
questions.explanation: The <select> element is used to create a drop-down list. It contains <option> tags representing available choices.

questions.question: What is the difference between <input type="text"> and <textarea>?
questions.a: <textarea> allows multiple lines of text input; type="text" is single-line
questions.b: <textarea> is used for code; type="text" is for regular writing
questions.c: type="text" has no character limit; <textarea> is limited to 255 characters
questions.explanation: The <textarea> tag defines a multi-line text input control, often used for comments or messages.

questions.question: Why might a developer choose the <button> tag over <input type="button">?
questions.b: <button> elements can wrap content like text, images, or icons; <input> cannot
questions.explanation: Because

questions.question: Which input type provides a native graphical color picker on supported browsers?
questions.explanation: <input type="color"> provides a native UI for selecting a color, submitting the value as a hex code (e.g., #ff0000).

questions.question: Which tag allows you to group related <option> elements within a <select> drop-down menu, creating a non-clickable header?
questions.explanation: The <optgroup> element groups related options in a drop-down list, labeled by its 'label' attribute.

questions.question: What does the <datalist> element do when connected to an <input>?
questions.a: It forces the user to pick only from a predefined list (like a standard select)
questions.b: It connects the input to an external database
questions.c: It provides a dropdown of autocomplete suggestions while still allowing custom typing
questions.d: It formats the input data into a table upon submission
questions.explanation: <datalist> provides an 'autocomplete' feature for <input> elements. Users see a drop-down of suggestions but can still type their own value.

questions.question: Which HTML5 input type provides a native slider control?
questions.explanation: <input type="range"> displays a slider control. It uses 'min' and 'max' attributes to define the range of numbers.

questions.question: Which tag is used to draw a visual box around related form elements and group them together?
questions.explanation: The <fieldset> element groups related data in a form and typically draws a box around them. It is often used with <legend>.

questions.question: Which attribute prevents a form from being submitted if the input field is left empty?
questions.explanation: The 'required' boolean attribute specifies that an input field must be filled out before submitting the form.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'placeholder' attribute?
questions.a: It sets the default value that gets submitted with the form
questions.b: It provides a short hint that is displayed in the input field before the user enters a value
questions.c: It reserves physical space for the input box on the screen
questions.d: It hides the input text for passwords
questions.explanation: The 'placeholder' attribute displays a temporary, greyed-out hint inside the input field that disappears once the user starts typing.

questions.question: What is the critical difference between the 'readonly' and 'disabled' attributes?
questions.a: Readonly fields are sent when the form submits; disabled fields are not sent
questions.b: Disabled fields can be focused by clicking; readonly fields cannot
questions.c: Readonly applies only to textareas; disabled applies to all inputs
questions.d: There is no difference in how the browser handles them
questions.explanation: A 'readonly' field cannot be modified but its value is still submitted. A 'disabled' field is unusable, unclickable, and its value is ignored upon submission.

questions.question: Which attribute limits the maximum number of characters a user can enter into a text input?
questions.explanation: The 'maxlength' attribute enforces a strict character limit on an input or textarea.

questions.question: What does the 'size' attribute control on an <input type="text">?
questions.a: The maximum number of characters allowed
questions.b: The visible width of the input field, measured in characters
questions.c: The font size of the typed text
questions.d: The maximum file size for an upload field
questions.explanation: The 'size' attribute specifies the visible width of an input element, typically in average character widths.

questions.question: Which attribute allows you to enforce a specific Regular Expression (Regex) that the input value must match?
questions.explanation: The 'pattern' attribute allows developers to define a regular expression the input's value is checked against on form submission.

questions.question: Which attributes are used together to specify the allowed numerical range for an <input type="number">?
questions.explanation: The 'min' and 'max' attributes specify the minimum and maximum allowed values for numerical and date inputs.

questions.question: Which attribute specifies the legal number intervals for an input field (e.g., only allowing multiples of 5)?
questions.explanation: The 'step' attribute dictates the legal number intervals (e.g., step="5" allows 0, 5, 10, 15).

questions.question: Which attribute automatically places the cursor inside a specific input field when the page loads?
questions.explanation: The 'autofocus' boolean attribute directs the browser to automatically focus that input control when the page finishes loading.

questions.question: How do you disable the browser's automatic suggestion drop-down for a specific input field?
questions.explanation: Setting autocomplete="off" prevents the browser from offering historical suggestions or saved credentials for that specific field.

questions.question: Which tag is used to display a completely separate web page within the current HTML document?
questions.explanation: The <iframe> (inline frame) is used to embed another document (like a YouTube video or external site) within the current HTML document.

questions.question: Which iframe attribute applies extra security restrictions on the content embedded within it?
questions.explanation: The 'sandbox' attribute enables an extra set of restrictions for the content in the iframe, such as blocking script execution or form submission.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the <script> tag?
questions.b: To embed or reference executable client-side code, typically JavaScript
questions.c: To display code snippets safely on the screen
questions.explanation: The <script> tag is used to embed client-side scripts (JavaScript) or point to an external script file using the 'src' attribute.

questions.question: What does the <noscript> element do?
questions.a: It instructs the browser to block all ads on the page
questions.b: It disables JavaScript for the entire document
questions.c: It provides alternative HTML content for users whose browsers do not support JavaScript or have it disabled
questions.d: It minifies JavaScript code before execution
questions.explanation: Content inside <noscript> is only rendered if the user's browser has JavaScript disabled or does not support client-side scripting.

questions.question: Which attribute on a <script> tag ensures that the external script is executed only after the HTML document has been completely parsed?
questions.explanation: The 'defer' attribute tells the browser to continue parsing the HTML and execute the script only after the DOM is fully built.

questions.question: Which tag was traditionally used to embed plug-ins like Flash or Java Applets, but is now rarely used?
questions.explanation: The <object> tag was heavily used to embed multimedia plug-ins. While still valid, HTML5's native video/audio elements have largely replaced it.

questions.question: When embedding an external script, which attribute is used to provide the file path?
questions.explanation: Just like an image, external scripts use the 'src' attribute (e.g., <script src="app.js"></script>).

questions.question: How is the <embed> tag different from <object> and <iframe>?
questions.a: It does not require a closing tag
questions.d: It only works for audio files
questions.explanation: The <embed> tag is an empty (void) element and therefore has no closing tag, unlike <object> and <iframe>.

questions.question: Which HTML5 element is used to embed sound files into a web page natively?
questions.explanation: The <audio> tag is the native HTML5 standard for embedding sound files.

questions.question: Which attribute must be added to <audio> or <video> tags to display play, pause, and volume buttons?
questions.explanation: Adding the boolean 'controls' attribute instructs the browser to display its native playback interface.

questions.question: Why is the <source> tag used inside <video> and <audio> elements?
questions.a: To allow the browser to choose from multiple file formats depending on its compatibility
questions.b: To apply external CSS styling to the media player
questions.c: To fetch the media file faster
questions.d: To define the copyright metadata of the media
questions.explanation: Providing multiple <source> tags (e.g., MP4 and WebM) ensures fallback support; the browser will play the first format it understands.

questions.question: Modern browsers block videos from playing automatically. How do you bypass this restriction using HTML attributes?
questions.c: Autoplay cannot be bypassed with HTML; it requires JavaScript
questions.explanation: Due to user experience policies, browsers block autoplaying media with sound. Adding the 'muted' attribute allows 'autoplay' to function silently.

questions.question: Which attribute on the <video> tag specifies an image to be shown while the video is downloading or until the user hits play?
questions.explanation: The 'poster' attribute takes a URL for an image to display before video playback begins.

questions.question: Which element is used to attach timed text tracks, such as subtitles or captions, to a <video>?
questions.explanation: The <track> element is placed inside <video> or <audio> to specify subtitles, caption files, or other text tracks.

questions.question: What does the 'loop' attribute do on a media element?
questions.a: It loops a specific 5-second section of the video
questions.b: It automatically restarts the media file from the beginning once it reaches the end
questions.c: It plays all media files on the page in a continuous sequence
questions.d: It reverses the playback once it finishes
questions.explanation: The boolean 'loop' attribute causes the audio or video to start over automatically every time it finishes.

questions.question: What is the correct way to handle browsers that do not support the <audio> element at all?
questions.a: There is no fallback; the page will crash
questions.b: Place fallback text directly between the <audio> and </audio> tags
questions.c: Use the 'fallback' attribute on the audio tag
questions.d: Redirect them to a different webpage automatically
questions.explanation: Any text placed between the opening and closing <audio> or <video> tags is displayed only if the browser doesn't recognize the element.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between HTML5 <canvas> and <svg>?
questions.a: Canvas is vector-based; SVG is raster/pixel-based
questions.b: Canvas draws graphics on the fly using JavaScript pixels; SVG defines vector graphics using XML tags
questions.c: Canvas is only for 3D; SVG is only for 2D
questions.d: Canvas is deprecated; SVG is the modern standard
questions.explanation: Canvas is a pixel-based raster drawing API manipulated via JavaScript. SVG is a resolution-independent vector format written in XML.

questions.question: Can you draw a rectangle inside a <canvas> element using only HTML tags?
questions.b: No, <canvas> acts only as a container; all drawing must be done via JavaScript
questions.d: No, rectangles require external image files
questions.explanation: The <canvas> tag itself is completely blank. Developers must use JavaScript (e.g., getContext('2d')) to actually draw shapes and pixels.

questions.question: Which tag creates a circle when placed inside an <svg> element?
questions.explanation: SVG uses straightforward XML tags like <circle>, <rect>, and <polygon> to render vector shapes directly in the DOM.

questions.question: Which HTML5 API allows a web application to find the user's physical longitude and latitude (if the user grants permission)?
questions.explanation: The HTML Geolocation API (accessed via navigator.geolocation in JS) is used to locate a user's position.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'localStorage' and 'sessionStorage' in HTML Web Storage?
questions.a: localStorage is secure; sessionStorage is not
questions.b: localStorage stores data with no expiration date; sessionStorage data is deleted when the browser tab is closed
questions.d: localStorage is for text; sessionStorage is for media
questions.explanation: sessionStorage is temporary and scoped to the specific browser tab. localStorage persists indefinitely until explicitly cleared.

questions.question: What is the purpose of HTML5 Web Workers?
questions.a: To scrape data from other websites
questions.b: To run JavaScript scripts in the background without affecting the performance of the UI/page
questions.c: To automatically update the HTML DOM
questions.d: To handle form validations on the server side
questions.explanation: Web Workers allow intense JavaScript execution on a separate thread, keeping the main web page responsive.

questions.question: How do you make a standard HTML element capable of being dragged by the user using the native HTML Drag and Drop API?
questions.explanation: Adding draggable="true" tells the browser that the user is allowed to click and drag the element.

questions.question: What does SSE stand for in the context of HTML5 APIs?
questions.explanation: Server-Sent Events (SSE) is an API that allows a web page to get automated, one-way updates from a server (like stock tickers or news feeds).

questions.question: When working with <canvas> in JS, what does canvas.getContext('2d') return?
questions.c: A drawing context object that provides methods and properties for drawing shapes and images
questions.d: The pixel width and height of the canvas
questions.explanation: getContext('2d') returns the built-in HTML5 object that holds the actual drawing methods (like fillRect, strokeText).

questions.question: Which of the following data types can Web Storage (localStorage/sessionStorage) natively store?
questions.explanation: The Web Storage API can only store string key/value pairs. To store objects, developers must use JSON.stringify() and JSON.parse().

questions.question: What does 'WCAG' stand for in web development?
questions.explanation: WCAG is the international standard outlining how to make web content more accessible to people with disabilities.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) attributes?
questions.b: To provide extra information and context to screen readers and assistive technologies
questions.c: To ensure forms are submitted securely
questions.explanation: ARIA attributes (like role="alert" or aria-hidden="true") act as an overlay to provide context missing from native HTML to assistive tech.

questions.question: What happens when you add aria-hidden="true" to an HTML element?
questions.a: It hides the element visually via CSS
questions.b: It hides the element entirely from screen readers, while leaving it visually visible
questions.c: It encrypts the text content inside the tag
questions.d: It prevents the user from highlighting the text
questions.explanation: aria-hidden="true" instructs screen readers to skip the element, which is useful for purely decorative icons or duplicate visual information.

questions.question: Which attribute allows you to make a non-interactive element (like a <div>) focusable using the keyboard's Tab key?
questions.explanation: Setting tabindex="0" inserts an element into the logical keyboard navigation flow, making it focusable.

questions.question: What is the HTML Character Entity used to display a 'less than' symbol (<) without the browser interpreting it as the start of a tag?
questions.explanation: The entity '<' stands for 'less than'. Using actual < signs in text can break HTML parsing.

questions.question: What does the character entity ' ' represent?
questions.explanation: A Non-Breaking Space ( ) creates a space between words that prevents the browser from breaking them apart onto separate lines.

questions.question: Why is URL Encoding necessary when sending data over the web?
questions.b: To ensure the server recognizes the doctype
questions.c: Because URLs can only be sent over the internet using the ASCII character set
questions.explanation: URLs must use the ASCII character set. Unsafe characters (like spaces) must be encoded (e.g., a space becomes %20 or +).

questions.question: What organization actively maintains the 'Living Standard' of HTML today?
questions.c: WHATWG (Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group)
questions.explanation: The WHATWG maintains the HTML Living Standard, having taken over primary governance from the W3C.

questions.question: When validating HTML code, what does the W3C Markup Validation Service primarily check for?
questions.a: Missing closing tags, invalid attributes, and structure violations
questions.d: The color contrast ratio for accessibility
questions.explanation: HTML Validators parse the DOM against the official specification to find syntax errors, improper nesting, and illegal attributes.

questions.question: According to accessibility standards, why is '<div> soup' (building a whole site using only <div> and <span> tags) considered harmful?
questions.b: It strips all semantic meaning from the page, making it impossible for screen readers to navigate via landmarks (like main, nav, header)
questions.c: It forces CSS to download slower
questions.d: It triggers infinite loops in JavaScript
questions.explanation: Without semantic tags (like <nav>, <main>, <button>), assistive technologies cannot provide structural context to visually impaired users.
